section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 1 of the Regulations relating to Banks (objective of Regulations and completeness of information) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.75
requirement: The bank must report all information required in every prescribed return completely and against the appropriate items and columns specified in each form, and must make available to the Prudential Authority, on request and within a reasonable period, an analysis of any information or item furnished in any prescribed return.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 2 of the Regulations relating to Banks (management accounts as basis for completion of returns)
requirement: The bank must prepare every prescribed return using the same principles used to prepare its management accounts and board reports, and must ensure each return is easily reconcilable to those management accounts and board reports; where the prescribed completion basis conflicts with the management-accounts basis, the bank must, after consultation, obtain the Prudential Authority's approval of the basis used.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 3 of the Regulations relating to Banks (Financial Reporting Standards)
requirement: The bank must prepare all prescribed returns in accordance with the Financial Reporting Standards in force from time to time (referring to IASB pronouncements where no specific standard or approved interpretation exists), apply the same accounting policy used in its annual financial statements, and where any authorised deviation occurs ensure the returns remain easily reconcilable to the annual financial statements.
fulfilmentPolicy: Regulatory Reporting Policy; Financial Reporting Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 3(4) of the Regulations relating to Banks (fair value option requirements)
requirement: Before first applying and on an ongoing basis whenever it adopts a fair value option or approach for financial instruments, the bank must have board-approved policies, procedures, robust risk-management systems and controls in place; must not apply the fair value option to instruments whose fair value it cannot reliably estimate; must have fair values and valuation models independently verified by a qualified unit independent of the originating business; and must subject the appropriateness of its fair value option use to periodic internal audit review.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 4(1)-(3) of the Regulations relating to Banks (certification of returns) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.75
requirement: The bank must, for every set of returns rendered, complete, sign and certify a form BA 099 signed by the chief executive officer, the chief accounting officer and the executive officer responsible for FIC Act compliance; where a signatory is unavailable, the officer performing that function must sign in an acting capacity with their normal office stated on the form.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 4(4)-(8) of the Regulations relating to Banks (rendition of returns) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.75
requirement: The bank must render every prescribed return, whether on the prescribed form or by electronic means, at the intervals prescribed in Chapter II (and Chapter VI), submit a completed form for the business it conducts in the Republic and for relevant business conducted elsewhere, and complete each return in the currency of the country in which the business is conducted or officially reported.

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 5 of the Regulations relating to Banks (failure or inability to comply) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.74
requirement: Whenever the bank fails or is unable to comply with any provision of the Regulations, it must report the failure or inability to the Prudential Authority in writing, stating the reasons, without waiting to be asked.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 7 of the Regulations relating to Banks (list of prescribed financial, risk-based and other related returns) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.75
requirement: The bank must submit to the Prudential Authority every financial, risk-based and other related return determined or directed in writing by the Authority, in accordance with the Authority's requirements, and within the submission periods prescribed (ranging from before 09:00 on the second business day after the reporting day, to 15, 20, 30, 60 or 90 days after the relevant period-end depending on the return).

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 18 of the Regulations relating to Banks (monthly balance sheet, form BA 100)
requirement: The bank must complete and submit the monthly balance-sheet return (form BA 100) in accordance with the instructions directed in writing by the Prudential Authority and with the Financial Reporting Standards in force, treating the return content as confidential.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 23 of the Regulations relating to Banks (credit risk, form BA 200) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must measure its credit-risk exposure and calculate the related minimum required capital and reserve funds using an approach adopted in accordance with the Regulations (simplified standardised, standardised, or - where approved - the foundation or advanced IRB approach), apply the prescribed credit-risk-mitigation rules, and complete and submit the monthly credit-risk return (form BA 200).
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 24(6) of the Regulations relating to Banks (large exposures / credit concentration) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.73
requirement: The bank must ensure that its exposure to any single counterparty or group of connected counterparties (other than a D-SIB, D-SIFI or G-SIB) does not at any time exceed 25 per cent of the sum of its qualifying common equity tier 1 and additional tier 1 capital and reserve funds, and that where the aggregate of its large exposures exceeds 800 per cent of that capital it holds any additional capital directed in writing by the Authority.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy; Large Exposures Policy

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 24(6)-(7) of the Regulations relating to Banks (large-exposure reporting, form BA 210) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.73
requirement: The bank must identify and report each large exposure - reporting exposure values before and after eligible credit-risk mitigation on the quarterly credit-risk return (form BA 210) - whenever an exposure, or the aggregate credit-concentration exposure, exceeds 10 per cent of the sum of its qualifying common equity tier 1 and additional tier 1 capital and reserve funds, and must consider possible connected counterparties (treating a group of connected counterparties as a single counterparty) on an economic-interdependence basis once its exposure to an individual counterparty exceeds 5 per cent of that capital.
fulfilmentPolicy: Large Exposures Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 24(6) of the Regulations relating to Banks (connected lending / lending to a related person)
requirement: The bank must subject any transaction with a related person, and the write-off of any related-party exposure exceeding 1 per cent of its qualifying common equity tier 1 capital and reserve funds, or otherwise posing special risks, to the prior written approval of the board of directors.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 26(12) of the Regulations relating to Banks (liquidity coverage ratio, form BA 300)
requirement: The bank must calculate and continuously maintain a Liquidity Coverage Ratio - an adequate stock of unencumbered level 1 and level 2 high-quality liquid assets sufficient to meet expected total net cash outflows over a 30-calendar-day severe liquidity-stress horizon - at not less than the minimum specified in writing by the Prudential Authority (the Basel III fully phased-in minimum of 100 per cent).
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 26(14) of the Regulations relating to Banks (net stable funding ratio, form BA 300)
requirement: The bank must calculate and on an ongoing basis maintain a Net Stable Funding Ratio - a minimum amount of stable funding relative to the liquidity profile of its assets and off-balance-sheet commitments over a one-year horizon - in accordance with Regulation 26(14) and any further conditions directed in writing by the Prudential Authority (the Basel III fully phased-in minimum of 100 per cent).

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 26 of the Regulations relating to Banks (liquidity risk, form BA 300)
requirement: The bank must measure and report its liquidity risk on the monthly liquidity return (form BA 300), including its contractual, business-as-usual and bank-specific-stress balance-sheet mismatches, potential concentrations of funding by significant counterparty, instrument and currency, available sources of stress funding, and its foreign-exchange contractual maturity ladder.
fulfilmentPolicy: Liquidity Risk Management Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 27(3) of the Regulations relating to Banks (minimum liquid assets, form BA 310) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.72(1)
requirement: The bank must hold, during each prescribed maintenance period, an average daily amount of level 1 high-quality liquid assets of not less than 5 per cent of its liabilities as reduced (per the latest monthly form BA 310), and must ensure its holding does not fall below 75 per cent of that average daily requirement at the close of any day, 50 per cent at any time during the day, with at least 95 per cent owned outright and unencumbered.

section: Domain I - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 27(2) of the Regulations relating to Banks (minimum reserve balance, form BA 310) read with South African Reserve Bank Act 90 of 1989 s.10A
requirement: The bank must hold and maintain the minimum reserve balance with the South African Reserve Bank determined under any Notice issued by the Governor under section 10A of the SARB Act, calculating the average daily amounts in accordance with Regulation 8, and complete the monthly form BA 310.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 28 of the Regulations relating to Banks (market / position risk, form BA 320) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must measure its exposure to market (position) risk arising from trading activities and specified banking activities and calculate the related minimum required capital and reserve funds using the standardised approach or, where approved by the Prudential Authority, an internal models approach, and complete and submit the monthly market-risk return (form BA 320).
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Risk Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain I - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 29(3) of the Regulations relating to Banks (net open foreign-currency position, form BA 325)
requirement: The bank must ensure that its aggregate effective net open foreign-currency position - in any single foreign currency and in all foreign currencies taken together - does not at the close of business on any day exceed the amount specified in writing by the Prudential Authority.
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Risk Policy; Treasury / FX Policy

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 29 of the Regulations relating to Banks (daily selected risk exposure, form BA 325)
requirement: The bank must determine and report on a daily basis, on form BA 325, its selected risk exposures arising from trading and treasury activities, including market (position) risk and related capital requirements, counterparty risk on trading-book positions, selected liquidity information, and currency risk on banking-book and trading-book positions.
fulfilmentPolicy: Market Risk Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 30 of the Regulations relating to Banks (interest-rate risk in the banking book, form BA 330)
requirement: The bank must measure the interest-rate risk in its banking book - including the repricing gap between assets and liabilities before and after derivatives, the impact on net interest income of prescribed interest-rate shocks, and the change in the net present value of its banking-book positions - and complete and submit the monthly IRRBB return (form BA 330).

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 32(4) of the Regulations relating to Banks (written derivatives policy)
requirement: The bank must have a board-approved written policy on derivative instruments that specifies the criteria for classifying derivatives as trading or banking activities, specifies the relevant transaction limits, and ensures derivative transactions are subject to adequate internal controls and appropriate internal audit coverage.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 32 of the Regulations relating to Banks (derivative instruments, form BA 350)
requirement: The bank must determine and report monthly, on form BA 350, the notional amounts of all derivative contracts transacted during the month and of all unexpired contracts, and the fair value of all unexpired contracts, distinguishing credit derivatives, risk categories, instrument types, OTC versus exchange-traded, and trading versus banking purpose.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 33 of the Regulations relating to Banks (operational risk, form BA 400) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must calculate its minimum required capital and reserve funds in respect of operational risk by reconciling its business-indicator components to its income-statement and balance-sheet items, and complete and submit the six-monthly operational-risk return (form BA 400).
fulfilmentPolicy: Operational Risk Policy; Capital Management Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 35(6) of the Regulations relating to Banks (securitisation schemes, form BA 500)
requirement: Whenever the bank invests in structured products or holds securitisation or resecuritisation exposures, it must conduct appropriate analysis of the underlying risks rather than relying solely on external credit ratings, track and aggregate credit risk and concentrations at transaction and business-line level, assess maturity mismatches and the impact of triggers on liquidity, earnings and capital, and report such exposures on the monthly form BA 500.
fulfilmentPolicy: Credit Risk Policy; Investment Risk Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 36 of the Regulations relating to Banks (consolidated supervision, form BA 600)
requirement: Where the bank forms part of a banking group with relevant subsidiaries or associates, it must calculate its consolidated qualifying capital, required capital and reserve funds and consolidated risk exposures (including credit concentration and market risk) on a consolidated basis, and complete and submit the quarterly consolidated-supervision return (form BA 600).
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Group Supervision Policy

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 38(8) of the Regulations relating to Banks (minimum required capital and reserve funds) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must at all times maintain qualifying capital and reserve funds against risk-weighted exposure of not less than the prescribed minima: common equity tier 1 capital of at least 4.5 per cent, total tier 1 capital of at least 6 per cent, and total qualifying capital of at least 8 per cent of risk-weighted exposure, or such higher percentage as the Authority determines.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 38(8)(e) of the Regulations relating to Banks (capital conservation and countercyclical buffers) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must hold, above the minimum capital ratios, a capital conservation buffer of 2.5 per cent of risk-weighted exposure met fully with common equity tier 1 capital, plus any countercyclical capital buffer (ranging between zero and 2.5 per cent of risk-weighted exposure) imposed in writing by the Authority, and must accept capital-distribution constraints (on dividends, buy-backs and bonuses) until any drawn-down buffer is restored.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 38(15) of the Regulations relating to Banks (leverage ratio) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must calculate a Basel III leverage ratio (tier 1 capital divided by the total exposure measure) to supplement its risk-based capital requirements and manage its business so that the leverage ratio is at no stage less than 4 per cent - equivalently a leverage multiple not exceeding 25 - and in no case less than 3 per cent, subject to any additional leverage-ratio buffer the Authority directs.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 38(8)(a) of the Regulations relating to Banks (systemic and idiosyncratic capital add-ons) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.70
requirement: The bank must hold, in addition to the minimum ratios and buffers, any further minimum capital percentage specified in writing by the Prudential Authority for systemic risk and any bank-specific (idiosyncratic / Pillar 2) capital add-on so specified, and (if and when designated systemically important) any additional loss-absorbency requirement directed by the Authority.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 38 of the Regulations relating to Banks (capital adequacy, leverage and TLAC, form BA 700)
requirement: The bank must calculate its aggregate risk-weighted exposure using the approaches it has adopted under the Regulations, apply the output floor (the higher of its calculated risk-weighted exposure and the prescribed phase-in percentage of risk-weighted exposure calculated under the standardised approaches), and complete and submit the monthly capital-adequacy, leverage and TLAC return (form BA 700).
fulfilmentPolicy: Capital Management Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 39(1)-(2) of the Regulations relating to Banks (process of corporate governance)
requirement: The bank's board of directors must establish and maintain an adequate and effective process of corporate governance - consistent with the nature, complexity and risk of the bank's on- and off-balance-sheet activities and responsive to changes in its environment - that includes the maintenance of effective risk management and capital management, and may appoint supporting committees to assist it.

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 39(4)-(5) of the Regulations relating to Banks (risk-management processes and policies)
requirement: The bank must have in place comprehensive board-approved policies, processes and procedures to identify, measure, monitor, control, price, mitigate and report each material risk it runs (including capital, credit, counterparty, concentration, market, interest-rate, liquidity, currency, operational, model/valuation and related-party risk), specifying relevant limits and allocated capital, ensuring breaches of internal limits are escalated and addressed, and adjusting the framework as its risk profile changes.
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Management Framework; Risk Appetite Statement

section: Domain A - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 39(5)(d) of the Regulations relating to Banks (stress testing and capital adequacy)
requirement: The bank must ensure its risk-management processes are robust enough to conduct regular stress-testing and scenario analysis, maintain sufficient liquidity and capital-adequacy buffers to remain solvent during prolonged periods of financial-market stress and illiquidity, conduct robust independent due diligence on its investments and exposures, and ensure new activities, instruments and products are reviewed and assessed by the relevant risk, control and business units before launch.
fulfilmentPolicy: Risk Management Framework; ICAAP; Stress Testing Policy

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 40 of the Regulations relating to Banks (conduct of directors)
requirement: The bank must ensure every director acquires a basic knowledge and understanding of the conduct of the business of a bank and of the laws, codes of conduct and customs governing such institutions, and that each director's competence is commensurate with the nature and scale of the business the bank conducts.

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 41 of the Regulations relating to Banks (composition of the board of directors)
requirement: The bank must ensure the chairperson of its board is not an employee of the bank, its subsidiaries or its controlling company and is not a member of the bank's or controlling company's audit committee, and that - absent the Authority's consent to a deviation - at least two members of the board are employees of the bank.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 43(1) of the Regulations relating to Banks (public disclosure)
requirement: The bank must disclose to the public, in its annual financial statements and other disclosures, reliable, relevant and timely qualitative and quantitative information enabling users to assess its financial condition, capital-adequacy position, liquidity position, financial performance, leverage ratio, ownership, governance, business activities, risk profile and risk-management practices.

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 43(1)(a) of the Regulations relating to Banks (board-approved disclosure policy)
requirement: The bank must have in place a formal board-approved disclosure policy that specifies the approach used to determine the materiality, nature and extent of information disclosed to the public, and that maintains appropriate internal control processes over, and regularly assesses the appropriateness of, the information disclosed.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 44 of the Regulations relating to Banks (annual financial statements)
requirement: The bank must compile its annual financial statements in accordance with the Financial Reporting Standards in force (referring to IASB pronouncements where no specific standard or interpretation exists), inform its auditors in writing of any authorised deviation, hold subsidiary financial statements available for the Authority on request, and prepare and submit interim reports in accordance with the relevant standards as soon as they become available.

section: Domain G - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 46 of the Regulations relating to Banks (audit reports)
requirement: The bank must ensure that, within 120 days of its financial year-end, its auditor reports to the Prudential Authority on the bank's prescribed returns (their reasonable reflection of the management accounts, completeness, accuracy and preparation per the Act and Regulations), on any significant weaknesses in internal controls over financial regulatory reporting and over lending and investment activities, and on the reconcilability of forms BA 100 and BA 900, facilitating the auditor's access to the relevant returns.
fulfilmentPolicy: External Audit Policy; Regulatory Reporting Policy

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 48 of the Regulations relating to Banks (internal audit)
requirement: The bank must establish an independent, objective and permanent internal audit function that evaluates and improves the effectiveness of its risk management, control, capital management and governance processes, forms an integral part of the ongoing monitoring of its internal controls and internal capital-assessment procedure, and supports (without substituting for) the board's ultimate responsibility for an adequate system of internal controls.

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 49(1)-(2) of the Regulations relating to Banks (compliance function)
requirement: The bank must have, as part of its risk-management framework and governance structure, an independent compliance function that continuously manages its regulatory and supervisory risk, headed by a senior compliance officer with adequate resources and stature and with authority to communicate directly and freely with the board, the audit committee and the external auditor, who functions independently of internal audit.

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 49(3) of the Regulations relating to Banks (compliance officer duties)
requirement: The bank's compliance officer must report directly to the board, audit committee and chief executive officer, submit a compliance report at every board or audit-committee meeting and provide the Authority with a copy, establish prompt mechanisms for reporting and resolving non-compliance, maintain a documented compliance monitoring programme, and compile and maintain a compliance manual that addresses all material risks and applicable legislation and is reviewed and updated at least once a year.

section: Domain F - Regulations Relating to Banks
citation: Regulation 55 of the Regulations relating to Banks (acquisition of shares in a bank or controlling company) read with Banks Act 94 of 1990 s.37
requirement: The bank must ensure that any acquisition of shares in the bank or its controlling company requiring the permission of the Registrar or Minister under section 37(2) of the Banks Act is the subject of an application on the prescribed form BA 007, accompanied by the prescribed written statement of the applicant's shareholdings and interests, before the acquisition proceeds.
fulfilmentPolicy: Corporate Governance Policy; Ownership / Shareholding Policy
